registration_kind: Public, code-frozen analysis preregistration after data acquisition and before comparison analysis; not third-party escrow

authorship_and_authorisation.protocol_drafted_by: Codex, red-teamed in a live Claude Fable 5 Max session, then mechanically encoded and tested by Codex
authorship_and_authorisation.founder_authorisation: The IGRM founder instructed the agents in chat to execute the maximum defensible IGRM release.
authorship_and_authorisation.founder_review_limit: The founder did not line-edit or separately sign this protocol before its public freeze.

attestation.scope: No joint statistic between any IGRM series and any AI-GPR series was computed in this execution session before this protocol and script were frozen.
attestation.limits: This is an execution-session attestation enforced by a public code freeze, not proof of blindness or a claim about unobserved activity outside this session.

source.name: Iacoviello-Tong AI-GPR country-monthly file
source.last_month_rule: The 2026-07-01 row is treated as July 2026, the last complete month available in the pinned bytes. The pin governs regardless of later provider revisions.
source.revision_note: The provider series can be revised. The exact file hash is therefore load-bearing.
source.citation: Iacoviello, Matteo and Jonathan Tong (2026), The AI-GPR Index: Measuring Geopolitical Risk using Artificial Intelligence.

igrm_inputs.series_definition: The inputs are the daily composite and five daily channel percentile columns in history.csv, never a 7-day or other smoothed series.

month_enters_if: IGRM composite has at least 15 non-missing daily observations in the calendar month.
AI-GPR India_all is non-missing in that calendar month.
The month is no later than 2026-07-01, the last complete month in the pinned bytes.
sample.other_series_missingness: Each descriptive or exploratory pair is analysed on its pairwise non-missing eligible months and reports its own n.
sample.month_list: Generated mechanically and published in full with the result; no hand edits are permitted.
sample.changes: Simple first differences only when both included observations are consecutive calendar months.

transformations.igrm_monthly: Arithmetic mean of the included daily percentile observations, separately for composite and each of the five channels.
transformations.ai_gpr: Used exactly as published in the four registered India columns.

statistics.P1_inferential_primary: Spearman rho between month-over-month changes of IGRM composite and AI-GPR India_all.
statistics.P2_descriptive_primary: Spearman rho in levels for IGRM composite and AI-GPR India_all. No decision language attaches because persistent levels may correlate mechanically.
statistics.S1_descriptive: Pearson equivalents of P1 and P2, for comparability with the standing GPRC_IND page.
statistics.S2_exploratory: A 6 by 4 Spearman table for IGRM composite plus five channels against India_all, India_initiator, India_respondent, and India_spillover, in levels and changes. Each cell reports n. No decision language attaches.
statistics.S3_descriptive: For each already registered IGRM episode in sample, publish the within-sample percentile rank of AI-GPR India_all in that event month. No AI-GPR hit rate is computed because the episode list was selected for IGRM's construct.
statistics.S4_divergence: Publish five level months selected greedily in descending absolute within-sample percentile-rank gap. After choosing a month, skip any immediately adjacent calendar month, then continue until five are selected. Ties retain chronological input order. Publish ranks and IGRM evidence links, never raw AI-GPR values.
statistics.qualitative_limit: Divergence rows may be described but not given causal interpretations.

inference.interval: Percentile 95% moving-block bootstrap interval for P1.
inference.runtime_seed_rule: The implementation initialises the generator with random_seed plus the block length.
inference.pairing: The two change series are resampled jointly; identical sampled time positions apply to both series in every draw.
inference.chain_breaks: Blocks never cross a non-consecutive calendar gap. Every full-length moving window in a segment is a candidate block. A segment shorter than the target block length is one whole candidate block.
inference.draw_rule: Candidate blocks are sampled uniformly with replacement, concatenated, and truncated to the original paired n. An undefined resampled rho is discarded and redrawn, leaving 10,000 defined draws.
inference.reported_diagnostics: Lag-1 autocorrelations for both primary level series and both primary change series.

decision_language.threshold_note: The 0.5 boundary is a registered descriptive convention, not a universal validation threshold.

rules_in_order.condition: rho < 0 and the 95% interval upper bound is below 0
rules_in_order.text: The measures diverge systematically; published as found, investigation registered separately.

rules_in_order.condition: the 95% interval lower bound is above 0 and rho >= 0.5
rules_in_order.text: Month-over-month movements in the two measures co-move substantially.

rules_in_order.condition: the 95% interval lower bound is above 0 and 0 < rho < 0.5
rules_in_order.text: The two measures share a common component but are far from redundant.

rules_in_order.condition: all other outcomes, including an interval containing 0
rules_in_order.text: At monthly frequency the two measures are largely distinct; divergence months are listed for inspection.

only_registered_discussion_frames: Corpus difference: the AI-GPR source uses three US newspapers while IGRM uses global GDELT coverage.
Construct difference: geopolitical risk intensity versus press-salience share.
Anchoring difference: a global country score versus India-specific fault-line channels.

robustness.R1_splice_sensitivity: When a complete splice-sensitivity history is published, rerun this identical frozen protocol on that series and report it beside the primary result.
robustness.R2_block_length: Repeat the P1 interval at a 12-month block length.

commit_sequence: Commit A publishes this registration, the frozen script, and enforcement tests, with no benchmark result.
Only after Commit A is public is the frozen script run against the pinned bytes.
Commit B publishes the verbatim generated aggregate/rank output, the complete month list, and a deviations log, without altering the script.
publication.result_fields: Aggregate correlations, intervals, sample metadata, ranks, IGRM links, and an explicit deviations list only.
publication.external_timestamp: Commit A should be anchored with an independent timestamp where operationally available; lack of one must be disclosed rather than silently implied.
